beats.vo: Last page, Lesson 8.4, The operating playbook: deploy, monitor, respond, review. Run every position through the same four-phase routine. Keep that page on the desk. This lesson adds one picture: Measure your results so deposits, withdrawals and lucky markets don't fool you.

Education only, not financial advice. Crypto and DeFi carry significant risk, including total loss of capital. This is general information. It does not consider your objectives, financial situation, or needs. Past or example results do not indicate future results. Consider independent advice. We do not sell or run a trading bot.
On-Chain Operator. Lesson 8.5, Measuring performance honestly. Navy and cyan. One idea at a time. You write it down. Education only.
You can already pull a number off a chain. The operating system is what you do with it: a register, a journal, and a kill rule.
Time-weighted return (TWR): chains the return of each period, ignoring when you added or removed money.
Money-weighted / simple gain: what your total capital actually did, including the timing of deposits.
Benchmark: compare against what you'd have got doing something simple: holding the same assets, or plain stablecoin lending.
Attribution: split the result into sources: price moves, fees, interest, incentives, costs, losses.
Work the example on paper. Start $100,000 → +10% in Q1 ($110,000) → deposit $50,000 ($160,000) → −5% in Q2 → $152,000. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.

Work the example on paper. defi_calc.py twr --period 10 --period -5 --start 100000 --end 152000 --net-deposits 50000 TWR: 1.10 × 0.95 − 1 = 4.50% (your decisions) Simple gain on $150,000 put in: 1.33% (hurt by the deposit landing before a down quarter) Then compare 4.50% with holding ETH over the same period, and with stablecoin lending. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.

Check yourself. 1. What does TWR remove? The answer: The effect of when deposits and withdrawals happened.
Check yourself. 2. Why use a benchmark? The answer: To see whether the strategy beat doing something simple, not just beat zero.
Check yourself. 3. Two quarters, +8% then +2%. TWR? The answer: 1.08 × 1.02 − 1 = 10.16%.
By the end of this lesson, you'll be able to measure your results so deposits, withdrawals and lucky markets don't fool you.
